description:
FOUND s491a (Opus) while measuring #1918 character by character
(scratch/s491a/probes/p1918.{pl,perl.out,pcl-before.out}, the R rows).
PRE-EXISTING on main 337f6a23 and NOT changed by #1918, which deliberately
touches only the NUMIFY side.

  perl 5.40.3                        perl    PCL
  "\x{ff11}\x{ff12}"  =~ /^\d+$/     TRUE    false
  "\x{661}\x{662}"    =~ /^\d+$/     TRUE    false
  "12\x{663}"         =~ /^\d+$/     TRUE    false
  "\x{1D7CE}"         =~ /^\d+$/     TRUE    false
  the same strings    =~ /^[0-9]+$/  false   false   (the ASCII class agrees)

perldoc perlrecharclass: "\d matches a single character considered to be a
decimal digit.  If the /a modifier is in effect, it matches [0-9]; otherwise
it matches the Unicode general category Nd."  So the two questions have
OPPOSITE answers and that is perl's own design: grok_number (numification) is
ASCII-only, the regex engine is Unicode-aware.  #1918 made the first of the
two right; this is the second.

WHY IT WAS LEFT: the regex engine's character classes are their own surface
(`\d` `\w` `\s` and their negations, POSIX classes, /a /u /l semantics), and a
one-character widening of `\d` alone would leave `\w` and the rest
inconsistent.  Measure the family before changing any of it.

BAR: `cl/` change -> full sweep + the re/ companion leg; guard rows beside the
#1918 ones in Pl/t/perf-levers-05.t (which record today's answers as the
NUMIFY side, so they do not move) plus a re- guard file.  The ASCII-class rows
(`[0-9]`) are the control: they must not move.
subject: `\d` in a regex does NOT match a non-ASCII decimal digit -- perl's `\d` matches every Unicode Nd without /a, so `"\x{661}\x{662}" =~ /^\d+$/` is TRUE in perl and FALSE in PCL (the mirror image of #1918, which was the numify side)
